The paper provides non-trivial lower bounds on performance metrics for absorptionless electromagnetic structures.
The method uses Lagrangian duality with a field constraint to derive bounds.
The field constraint is on the norm of the electric field inside the device.
The parameter α controls the maximum allowed field intensity relative to a reference field.
The field constraint α is calculated using the Green's function and contrast limits.
For TE scattering, the bound remains finite for all contrast values.
For TM scattering, the bound diverges for negative permittivity materials.
The bound d(α) represents the minimum achievable performance metric given the field constraint.
The method is applied to 2D dielectric and metallic scatterers.
The optimization problem is discretized using pulse-basis and delta-testing functions.
The Fenchel dual is used to transform the problem into a convex dual.
The bounds are close to locally optimized results for small contrast or small design regions.
The bounds may deviate for larger contrasts or regions when the field constraint is loose.
The method can be integrated with other approaches for absorptive structures.
The Green's function describes the background electromagnetic environment.
The method helps determine fundamental limits of scattering performance for lossless devices.
The paper includes numerical studies of convergence for the discretized problem.
The bounds are derived for both transverse electric and transverse magnetic scattering.
The method is general and can be extended to other wave-scattering problems.

The method is not specialized to electromagnetic scattering and can be applied to other fields like acoustics or quantum physics.
The paper references several previous works on bounds for electromagnetic structures.
The method is illustrated with examples of 2D scatterers in vacuum.
The bounds depend on the choice of design region and contrast limits.
